rfi.title: France counts the cost of violence and looting during day of action
rfi.description: French authorities and businesses were on Sunday assessing the extent of the damage after demonstrations involving 550,000 people nationwide descended into violence and looting.

rfi.title: Ebola vaccine trials 'reason for hope' in DR Congo and beyond
rfi.description: Five months into the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, there is still no approved vaccine against the rare Bundibugyo strain that has now caused more than 4,000 deaths. But candidates currently undergoing trials give reason to hope, according to Emanuele Capobianco of Gavi, the global vaccine alliance.

rfi.title: Three years on from Kenya's Shakahola cult murders, families still seek closure
rfi.description: A court in Mombasa, Kenya, will on Monday deliver a long-awaited verdict in the Shakahola sect murder trial. Paul Nthenge Mackenzie, a self-proclaimed pastor, is accused of forcing church members, including children, to starve themselves to death in order to meet Jesus. Three years after the tragedy, families of the victims are hoping for closure so they can finally mourn their loved ones.

rfi.title: Poison and remedy: secrets of the botanic garden at Paris's Pharmacy Faculty
rfi.description: A stone's throw from the Jardin du Luxembourg on Paris's Left Bank, the Faculty of Pharmacy is home to a botanical garden which serves as an educational resource for students and a space for research – as well as a place where visitors can find biodiversity in the heart of the city.

rfi.title: France's new sexual violence bill 'fails to tackle root causes', campaigners warn
rfi.description: A sweeping package of reforms, passed unanimously by the lower house of parliament this week, aims to overhaul how France investigates and prosecutes sexual violence. Yet campaigners say the legislation does not do enough to prevent abuse, while protection for some of the most vulnerable victims is lacking.

rfi.title: AI midwife seeks to fill gaps in Zimbabwe's maternal health care
rfi.description: With public health services stretched thin, women in Zimbabwe sometimes struggle to access reliable information about pregnancy and childbirth. A locally developed app aims to answer their questions and direct them to appropriate care, in an example of the potential of artificial intelligence to ease pressure on overloaded health systems.

rfi.title: Pacific nations await climate billions, as fossil fuel divide looms over Cop31
rfi.description: Ahead of next month’s United Nations Cop31 climate summit, as a strengthening El Niño drives Pacific sea temperatures towards record levels, more than $5 billion promised to the region remains unpaid. Cop31 co-hosts Turkey and Australia are pushing to speed up the switch to electric transport, heating and industry, but participating countries are divided over how to wind down the use of coal, oil and gas.

rfi.title: Shipping attacks threaten Turkey's resolve to keep warships out of Black Sea
rfi.description: A wave of deadly attacks on cargo ships in the waters of NATO members Bulgaria and Romania has jolted the alliance into calling an emergency meeting on Black Sea security. Yet any move to send NATO ships hinges on Turkey reversing its steadfast refusal to allow warships into the Black Sea.

rfi.title: Zelensky says US move to waive sanctions 'rewards' Russia's Putin
rfi.description: Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky on Saturday hit out at the decision of the US President Donald Trump to block sanctions on Russia claiming the move rewarded the country's leader Vladimir Putin.

rfi.title: Madagascar marks one year since uprising as Russia’s influence grows
rfi.description: Madagascar marks one year on Saturday since military leader Michael Randrianirina took power following weeks of youth-led protests that brought down elected president Andry Rajoelina. Over the past year, Russian influence has grown through closer military ties and weapons deliveries, while researchers have identified Moscow’s interest in a strategic Indian Ocean port. Many of the political reforms demanded by protesters, however, remain unfinished.

rfi.title: Mayors urge France to recognise 1961 Paris massacre of Algerians as state crime
rfi.description: On the eve of the 65th anniversary of the massacre of Algerian protesters in Paris, French mayors are calling for the events of 17 October, 1961 to be officially recognised as a state crime.

rfi.title: School students called to join Yellow Vests and unions for mass French protest
rfi.description: Following an unsuccessful meeting with France's education minister on Thursday, protesting high school pupils across the country say they will not let up the pressure on the government. The Yellow Vests movement has called on the students to join them at a nationwide demonstration on Saturday over working conditions and the cost of living.

rfi.title: France and Germany strike deal to boost Europe's struggling car industry
rfi.description: France and Germany have agreed a deal to safeguard Europe's automobile industry and stave off fierce competition from Chinese electric car companies. The agreement also opens the door for the United Kingdom to be treated as a trusted partner under "Made in EU" rules.

rfi.title: Nineteen injured as minibus crashes into Channel Tunnel shuttle train
rfi.description: A minibus carrying truck drivers crashed into a freight train at the loading platform of the Eurotunnel injuring 19 people, French authorities said.

rfi.title: Somalia sets date for May presidential election amid ongoing Islamist insurgency
rfi.description: Somalia's election commission has announced it will hold parliamentary and presidential polls in April and May next year, but critics say the decision will lead to more conflict in a deeply fragmented country facing a long-running Islamist insurgency.

rfi.title: Infantino offers apology but 'no answers' at Fifa meeting over World Cup plan
rfi.description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino gave "no satisfactory answers" when grilled Thursday during a meeting to discuss his attempts to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors, senior members of football's global governing body said, but he did offer an apology for the failed project.

rfi.title: Challenge to HIV restrictions in French armed forces goes before top court
rfi.description: Several organisations have brought a case before France’s highest court to challenge the continued exclusion of people living with HIV from certain posts in the armed forces, gendarmerie and fire services.

rfi.title: Trial of French IS returnee highlights a growing focus on the women who came back
rfi.description: Courts are increasingly turning their attention to the women who joined the Islamic State armed group in Syria and Iraq, and then returned to France. The latest case opened Wednesday: that of Radia Tahar Aouidate, was one of 23 members of her family to travel to Syria, under the influence of her brother.

euronews.description: Huge plumes of black smoke billowed over St Petersburg, Russia’s second-largest city, on Sunday, 18 October, as a large-scale Ukrainian drone attack sparked fires at industrial and logistics facilities. lemonde.description: A l’approche des élections législatives israéliennes du 27 octobre, plusieurs ONG décrivent les méthodes des extrémistes religieux pour chasser les Palestiniens de leurs terres et les entraves à la cueillette des olives par les colons.

lemonde.title: En Californie, la tournée au pas de course de Gabriel Zucman pour taxer les milliardaires
lemonde.description: L’économiste franco-américain de 39 ans est parti livrer bataille en Californie, alors que les élections de mi-mandat approchent. Son objectif : faire voter, le 3 novembre, lors d’un référendum, une mesure qui permettrait d’imposer ponctuellement 5 % du patrimoine des milliardaires qui résident dans cet Etat. Un militantisme qui, selon certains de ses collègues, prend le pas sur sa démarche scientifique.

lemonde.title: A Aix-en-Provence, le procès d’un triple homicide qui a préfiguré la montée en puissance de la DZ Mafia
lemonde.description: En 2020, trois hommes ont été assassinés, dont le demi-frère du militant contre le narcotrafic Amine Kessaci. Parmi les accusés renvoyés devant la cour d’assises à partir de lundi se trouve notamment Amine Oualane, considéré aujourd’hui comme l’un des leaders du groupe criminel marseillais.

lemonde.title: Comment l’administration de Donald Trump utilise des pays africains pour expulser des migrants en dépit du droit international
lemonde.description: Sur les 28 000 immigrés expulsés des Etats-Unis entre le début de 2025 et août 2026, plus de 500 ont été envoyés sur le continent africain, selon les données du Deportation Data Project. La plupart du temps, ils n’ont pas de lien direct avec les pays d’Afrique.

lemonde.description: Faute d’accord entre le Frente Amplio et Podemos, les formations situées à la gauche du Parti socialiste ouvrier espagnol se présenteront séparément dans la plupart des circonscriptions. Une division qui risque de peser lourd dans les urnes.

lemonde.title: Pour l’essayiste états-unien Thomas Chatterton Williams, « la gauche américaine a commis une erreur majeure en défendant une politique centrée sur l’identitarisme »

lemonde.description: Le président ukrainien, Volodymyr Zelensky, a fait savoir, dans un entretien à l’émission « Meet the Press » de NBC, diffusé dimanche, que les Etats-Unis transmettaient de nouveau des renseignements à l’Ukraine après une interruption pendant « un certain temps ». M. Zelensky a également dit espérer que des discussions avec Washington puissent se tenir cette semaine.

lemonde.title: Le pape Léon XIV remercie les fidèles réunis place Saint-Pierre après son opération et annonce la reprise progressive de ses activités
lemonde.description: Léon XIV, 71 ans, a été opéré mardi à l’hôpital Gemelli de Rome où on lui a retiré un nodule cancéreux au poumon droit, et il a été autorisé à sortir de l’hôpital samedi. Ses médecins ont affirmé qu’il s’était rétabli rapidement et devrait pouvoir reprendre ses voyages.

lemonde.title: Dans l’Aisne, Paul Mougenot, le sénateur inclassable, admirateur de Charles Maurras, embarrasse aussi bien à droite qu’à l’extrême droite
lemonde.description: Elu à la surprise générale lors des élections sénatoriales le 27 septembre, cet ancien collaborateur de l’Action française a été exclu de la droite locale, avant de se voir refuser l’investiture du Rassemblement national. Sans attache, le conseiller départemental siège parmi les non-inscrits.

lemonde.title: Du flamenco sur un air de Rosalia, les champions olympiques Guillaume Cizeron et Laurence Fournier Beaudry continuent d’élargir l’horizon du patinage artistique
lemonde.description: Le couple, qui a remporté l’or en février aux Jeux de Milan-Cortina, doit faire son retour à la compétition fin octobre lors du Grand Prix de France. Pour l’occasion, il dévoilera ses nouveaux programmes, dont le court a été imaginé sur une musique de la chanteuse catalane.

lemonde.description: La société Unit1 Studio veut créer les avatars numériques de musiciens disparus ou trop âgés pour se produire sur scène. Et espère par la suite les envoyer en tournée.

lemonde.title: A la Comédie-Française, Julie Duclos ou l’art du théâtre qui va de soi

lemonde.title: « Une vie pour l’art. Gustave Fayet » : portrait d’un collectionneur clairvoyant
lemonde.description: Diffusé à l’occasion de l’exposition qui lui est consacrée à la Fondation Louis Vuitton, à Paris, ce documentaire de Nadège de Peganow révèle la personnalité complexe de celui qui se voulait aussi artiste.

france24fr.title: 17 octobre : policiers et experts décrivent une situation "dramatique"
france24fr.description: "Etat dépassé", "mauvaise anticipation", "dispositif policier sous-dimensionné", défaut "de réponse politique": au lendemain d'une mobilisation contre la "vie chère" émaillée de violences et pillages, élus, policiers et experts décrivent une situation "dramatique" qui dépasse le seul enjeu du maintien de l'ordre en France.

france24fr.title: Manifestations du 17 Octobre : Emmanuel Macron prendra la parole à 20h
Macron s'adressera aux Français après les violences en marge des manifestations

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : regain de tension à Paris, la brigade d'intervention CRS 8 à nouveau déployée
17 octobre : au lendemain des violences, le gouvernement sous forte pression
france24fr.description: Appels à la "démission" du ministre de l'Intérieur, critiques sur la stratégie de maintien de l'ordre: l'exécutif était sous forte pression dimanche au lendemain des violences en marge des manifestations du 17 octobre. En retrait jusqu'ici, Emmanuel Macron va s'adresser aux Français à 20h.

france24fr.title: Un siècle après son vol, le diamant rose dévoile toute ses facettes au château de Chantilly
france24fr.description: Joyau historique ayant appartenu à la famille de Louis II de Bourbon-Condé, cousin de Louis XIV, le diamant rose est exposé depuis le 17 octobre, une première depuis près d'un siècle et son vol au château de Chantilly en 1926. Archives inédites, photographies, coupures de presse et analyses scientifiques retracent les multiples vies de cette pierre d'exception.

france24fr.title: Mobilisation du 17 octobre : la police dépassée par les évènements ?
france24fr.description: Axel Ronde, brigadier-chef de police, président et porte-parole du syndicat de Police CFTC, est notre invité.

france24fr.title: Cancer du sein en France : recherches cruciales et traitements alternatifs
france24fr.description: Toulsie Ramtohul, radiologue à l'Institut Curie, est notre invité.

france24fr.title: Mobilisations massives du 17 octobre : qui sont les casseurs ?
france24fr.description: Le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu va présider lundi à 10H00 une cellule interministérielle de crise, au surlendemain des violences qui ont éclaté en marge des manifestations du 17 octobre, a annoncé Matignon.Cette réunion devait initialement avoir lieu dimanche à 19H00, mais Matignon a annoncé son report pour des questions d'"agenda".

france24fr.title: 17 octobre : la France face aux stigmates de violences inédites
france24fr.description: Johan Bodin est en direct de la place de la République à Paris.

france24fr.description: Flavien Bénazet, Secrétaire Général du syndicat SNUIPN-FSU, est notre invité.

Mobilisation en France, manifestations en Albanie, violences en Cisjordanie : la semaine en images
france24fr.description: Retour sur les temps forts de l'actualité de la semaine écoulée et sur ses images les plus marquantes : le mouvement lycéen et la mobilisation du 17 octobre en France, l'attaque au fusil perpétrée dans un collège à Aubagne, le naufrage meurtrier d'une embarcation de migrants au large de Djibouti ou encore les manifestations contre le pouvoir en Albanie.

Des milliers de Russes et d'Ukrainiens privés électricité après de nouvelles frappes croisées
france24fr.description: Plusieurs attaques contre des cibles énergétiques en Russie et en Ukraine perpétrées dans la nuit de samedi à dimanche ont privé des milliers de Russes et d'Ukrainiens d'électricité. Des frappes de drones ukrainiennes ont notamment touché le Terminal pétrolier de Saint-Pétersbourg, suscitant d'impressionnants incendies sur ce site.

france24fr.title: 17 octobre : 800 000 participants en France, selon un bilan actualisé
france24fr.description: Quelque 800.000 personnes ont participé aux actions et défilés partout en France samedi contre la "vie chère", selon un bilan actualisé diffusé par plusieurs organisations associées à cette mobilisation nationale.

france24fr.title: 17 octobre : pillages, chaos, les forces de l'ordre dépassées ?
france24fr.description: Le gouvernement de Sébastien Lecornu est dimanche la ⁠cible de critiques ​sur sa gestion du maintien de l'ordre au lendemain des scènes de violence et de pillages qui ont terni une journée de vaste mobilisation contre la ​vie chère dans toute la France.

france24fr.title: Violences à Paris : plus de 500 personnes en garde à vue, annonce le parquet
france24fr.description: Plus de 500 personnes (517) sont en garde à vue dimanche après les violences et pillages commises samedi à Paris, plus précisément 346 personnes majeures et 171 mineurs, a indiqué le parquet de la capitale dans un bilan "pas encore consolidé".

zeit.description: Die Ukraine erhält bei der Raketenabwehr laut Selenskyj wieder Unterstützung der US‑Dienste. Der Präsident warnte eindringlich vor einem dauerhaften Entzug von US-Hilfen.

zeit.title: Christa Pike: »Nach internationalem Menschenrecht ist Christa Pike ein Folteropfer«
zeit.description: Was folgt aus der missglückten Hinrichtung der verurteilten Mörderin? Ein Gespräch mit ihrer Anwältin – und mit einer prominenten Gegnerin der Todesstrafe.

zeit.title: Heidi Levine: »Ich habe jeden Tritt gespürt«
zeit.description: Die US-Fotografin Heidi Levine wollte im Westjordanland die Gewalt durch Siedler dokumentieren. Dann wurde sie selbst attackiert. Hier spricht sie über den Vorfall.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Neue Ausschreitungen in Paris – Polizei setzt Tränengas ein
spiegel.description: Nach den Exzessen des Vortages kommt es in Paris erneut zur Gewalt. Am Platz der Republik werden Geschäfte geplündert, wieder sind Sondereinheiten der Polizei im Einsatz.

spiegel.title: Wahl in Israel: Donald Trump wirbt für Benjamin Netanyahu
spiegel.description: Knapp anderthalb Wochen vor der Parlamentswahl in Israel hat US-Präsident Trump eine Wahlempfehlung für den Amtsinhaber Netanyahu ausgesprochen. Er sei ein »Partner für Frieden«.

spiegel.title: Rechtsextremismus: Unterwegs in der Welt der »Reichsbürger« – Staatsschützer warnen vor einflussreichem »Ewigen Bund« – SPIEGEL TV
spiegel.description: Sie nennen sich »Ewiger Bund«, lehnen das Grundgesetz ab, haben eigene Ämter und Gesetze. Und sie glauben zu wissen, wer ab 2030 regieren wird.

spiegel.title: Tischtennis: Annett Kaufmann wird Vize-Europameisterin in Ljubljana
spiegel.description: Einzelgold blieb Annett Kaufmann bei der EM in Ljubljana verwehrt. Ihren rasanten Aufstieg setzt die deutsche Tischtennishoffnung dennoch fort. Begonnen hat er bei Olympia, zunächst in der Rolle als Ersatzspielerin.

spiegel.title: Mahnmal »Gleis 17«: Kai Wegner und Ron Prosor gedenken jüdischen Opfern im Nationalsozialismus
spiegel.description: Vor 85 Jahren begannen die Deportationen von Jüdinnen und Juden aus Berlin. Am Mahnmal »Gleis 17« gedachte Bürgermeister Wegner der Opfer. Andere warnten vor einem neu aufflammenden Antisemitismus.

spiegel.title: KZ-Gedenkstätten: Rechtsextreme Vorfälle häufen sich – zu Besuch in Ravensbrück
spiegel.description: In KZ-Gedenkstätten häufen sich rechtsextreme Vorfälle, auch in Ravensbrück. Wird die Verhöhnung der Naziverbrechen zur Normalität?

spiegel.title: Fußball-Bundesliga: SC Freiburg verliert in Leverkusen – FC Bayern neuer Spitzenreiter
spiegel.description: Der SC Freiburg verliert bei Bayer Leverkusen und muss die Tabellenführung an den FC Bayern abgeben. Auch Tennisbälle konnten die Werkself nicht aufhalten. Und: Jürgen Klopp hatte auf der Tribüne gut lachen.

spiegel.title: Premier League: Brighton & Hove Albion trifft von der Mittellinie – Fabian Hürzelers Team nun Zweiter
spiegel.description: Brighton & Hove Albion überrollt Crystal Palace: Nach zehn Minuten stand es bereits 3:0, ein Tor fiel aus gut 50 Metern. Mit diesem nächsten Sieg ist das Team von Fabian Hürzeler vorerst Zweiter der Premier League.

spiegel.title: Keltengrab in Baden-Württemberg: Illegale Schatzsucher in der Riedlinger Totenkammer
spiegel.description: Auf einem Acker in Baden-Württemberg haben Archäologen ein geplündertes Keltengrab entdeckt. Detektivisch rekonstruierten die Forscher, wie die Räuber vorgingen.

spiegel.title: Südkorea: Hilfe für Kinder aus Nordkorea – warum eine Schule für Geflüchtete angefeindet wird
spiegel.description: An der Yeomyung-Schule in Südkorea finden traumatisierte nordkoreanische Jugendliche zurück ins Leben. Doch gegen einen neuen Campus gibt es Proteste der Anwohner – das erzählt viel über das Verhältnis von Nord und Süd.

spiegel.title: Ukraine: USA liefern der Ukraine laut Selenskyj wieder Daten zur Abwehr von Raketenangriffen
spiegel.description: Nach einer Unterbrechung geben die Vereinigten Staaten nach Angaben von Wolodymyr Selenskyj wieder Geheimdienstinformationen an die Ukraine weiter. Zugleich zeigte sich der ukrainische Präsident besorgt über den US-Kurs gegenüber Moskau.

spiegel.title: Westjordanland: EU fordert Konsequenzen nach Angriff auf Diplomatenkonvoi
spiegel.description: Nach dem Angriff radikaler Siedler auf einen Konvoi mit Diplomaten fordert die EU Konsequenzen. Israels Ministerpräsident Netanyahu spricht unterdessen von einer »Verleumdungskampagne« gegen Siedler.

spiegel.title: Hitzewallungen: Was gegen Wechseljahrsbeschwerden hilft – neueste Erkenntnisse
spiegel.description: In den Wechseljahren verändert sich etwas im Körper, das bemerken die meisten Frauen. Manche kommen damit gut zurecht, andere brauchen Hilfe. Eine Gynäkologin erklärt, was Linderung verschafft.

spiegel.title: Repaircafé Eberswalde: Reparatur als »Glücksmoment, wie wenn ein dicker Fisch anbeißt«
spiegel.description: Frank Menge, 68, rettet im Repaircafé in Eberswalde ehrenamtlich Laptops, Akkuschrauber und Bügeleisen. Seine Erfolgsquote ist hoch – wie läuft das ab?

spiegel.title: Linke, Grüne, SPD in Berlin: Berliner Regierungsbildung belastet Koalition im Bund
spiegel.description: In Berlin wird eine Koalition aus Linken, Grünen und SPD immer wahrscheinlicher. CSU-Chef Markus Söder und andere in der Union schäumen, auch in der Bundes-SPD wächst die Kritik. Die Bundesregierung hat ein Problem mehr.

spiegel.title: Fußball in Hamburg: Spieler aus Ghana in Finnland wegen Vergewaltigung verurteilt, Empörung in der Bezirksliga
spiegel.description: Ein ghanaischer Fußballer ist in Finnland wegen Vergewaltigung verurteilt worden, rechtskräftig ist das Urteil aber noch nicht. In Hamburg spielt er nun in der Bezirksliga, das gefällt den gegnerischen Teams nicht.

spiegel.title: »Tatort« heute aus Kiel: »Unter Feinden« im Schnellcheck
spiegel.description: Gewalt als Teambuildingmaßnahme? Almila Bagriacik und Karoline Schuch müssen im Kampf gegen Mafia und Korruption zusammenfinden. Abschluss der »Tatort«-Neuaufstellung an der Förde.

spiegel.title: Sankt Petersburg: Aufnahmen zeigen Brände nach Drohnenangriffen
spiegel.description: Russland meldet mehr als 100 abgeschossene ukrainische Drohnen. Doch auf ersten verifizierten Videos sind Explosionen und Brände in Putins Heimatstadt zu sehen.

observador.title: Endometriose. Portugueses tentam acelerar diagnóstico
observador.description: Susana demorou 12 anos a ser diagnosticada com endometriose. Um projeto europeu, que conta com presença portuguesa em Braga, quer reduzir essa espera para um ou dois meses.

observador.title: Paris. Polícia de choque mobilizada para novas pilhagens
observador.description: É na Praça da República que estão concentrados os confrontos entre centenas de pessoas e as forças de segurança. Macron irá falar ao país.

observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Mortes nas manifestações? “Cada um tem de meter a mão na ...
observador.description: "Morte é morte", venha de onde vier, frisa antigo Presidente moçambicano. Não se deve causar "distúrbios que não se possam controlar", avisa. E diz a Mondlane: "Um não é mais povo do que o outro".

observador.title: 16h. Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro debatem hoje pela 1º vez
observador.description: O frente a frente está marcado para a meia-noite, hora de Lisboa. Ainda, manifestantes acampados em Lisboa e no Porto pretendem manter-se em protesto ao longo do dia de hoje.

observador.title: IL realiza Convenção Nacional no final de janeiro
observador.description: Partido marcou a XI Convenção para os dias 30 e 31 de janeiro de 2027, em Lisboa.

observador.title: Os candelabros da baixela Germain que regressam a Portugal
observador.description: Parte do conjunto de mais de mil peças encomendado por D. José I ao ourives de Luís XV, as peças foram adquiridas recentemente por colecionadores portugueses, por 3,4 milhões de euros.

observador.title: O que ninguém quer ver despediu Amorim mas aguenta Carrick?
observador.description: Lisandro lançou "bomba" em Madrid, estilhaços chegaram a vários lados, Carrick mantém-se seguro. Porquê? Ninguém sabe: após empatar onde Amorim disse adeus, United tem sete pontos em sete jogos (1-1).

observador.title: O "xadrez" que vai reconfigurar o BCE com a saída de Lagarde
observador.description: Reuters noticiou que saída antecipada pode consumar-se já nas próximas semanas. Lagarde queria "águas calmas" para sair mas deverá ter de fazê-lo no meio da turbulência que envolve o seu país-natal.

observador.title: Madeira. JPP denuncia listas de espera cinco anos
observador.description: O maior partido da oposição na Madeira considera inadmissível que ainda existam cidadãos à espera de consultas, exames ou cirurgias há mais de cinco anos.

observador.title: Maja Chwalinska vence WTA 1.000 de Wuhan
observador.description: A polaca, que foi finalista na última edição de Roland Garros, venceu o WTA 1.000 de Wuhan depois de derrotar Sonay Kartal por 2-6, 6-4 e 6-2.

observador.title: 15h. Porto. Luísa Neto pede explicações sobre carga policial
observador.description: Numa nota à imprensa, Luísa Neto diz que vai avaliar se a intervenção da PSP foi, ou não, compatível com o direito de reunião e manifestação. Ainda, preços dos combustíveis voltam a sofrer alterações.

observador.title: Miguel fechou com um top 10 que não chegou para o top 10
observador.description: Três pódios, sete top 6, 14 top 10: Miguel Oliveira fechou ano de rookie no Mundial de Superbike pela BMW em décimo na corrida 2 em Espanha, acabando no 11.º lugar de um Mundial dominado pela Ducati.

observador.title: "A Caça ao Estripador de Lisboa": o que é o teatro imersivo?
observador.description: O espectáculo estreia-se a 28 de outubro, a partir de um podcast do Observador. Mas como é que a "imersão" é um dos protagonistas? Quais os maiores desafios? E até que ponto se pode tornar tendência?

observador.title: Trump culpa a imigração pelos distúrbios em França
observador.description: Presidente norte-americano pronunciou-se sobre os protestos violentos em França, culpando a imigração. "Fechem as fronteiras", pediu aos franceses.

observador.title: Filipe Toledo e Nadia Erostarbe vencem sessão em Supertubos
observador.description: Brasileiro Filipe Toledo e espanhola Nadia Erostarbe ganharam a sessão livre de surf da prova da elite mundial na Praia de Supertubos, em Peniche.

observador.title: 14h. UE condena ataques dos colonos a diplomatas europeus
observador.description: A nota de repúdio foi conhecida hoje em comunicado da porta voz da UE para os negócios estrangeiros. E ainda, novo Ministro da Defesa do Irão promete ripostar contra vizinho, caso EUA ataquem.

observador.title: Carla Madeira e a ambiguidade moral do amor materno
observador.description: Antes, houve "Tudo é Rio", "A Natureza da Mordida" e "Véspera". Agora é a vez de "Quando": quando uma mãe vive a dúvida de denunciar ou não o filho? E nós bem no epicentro da narrativa.

nzz.title: Den EHC Kloten und die ZSC Lions trennen nach zwölf Runden sagenhafte 24 Punkte
nzz.description: Der bemitleidenswerte Tabellenletzte Kloten verliert in Lausanne 2:5, es ist die zehnte Niederlage in den letzten elf Partien. So schlecht ist Kloten seit dem Abstiegsjahr 2017/18 nie mehr in eine Saison gestartet.

nzz.title: Iran-Krieg steht vor neuer Eskalation: Benzinpreise in der Schweiz ziehen an
nzz.description: Die Treibstoffpreise steigen in der Schweiz wegen des Konflikts im Nahen Osten und Trumps «Diesel-Deal» stark. Konsumenten sollten sich langfristig auf hohe Energiepreise einstellen.

nzz.title: Elisabeth Baume-Schneider am SP-Parteitag: «Die Kritik an der höheren Mehrwertsteuer ist eine Nebelpetarde»
nzz.description: Die Delegierten lancieren die Initiative zum Schutz vor Gewalt an Frauen. Auch die Mehrwertsteuererhöhung zur Finanzierung der 13. AHV-Rente ist ein Thema. Elisabeth Baume-Schneider kritisiert die Gegner scharf.

nzz.title: Gegen «Linke und Heimatmüde»: Die SVP feiert an der Delegiertenversammlung sich selbst
nzz.description: Die Delegierten der SVP fassten am Samstag in Bulle die Parolen für die Abstimmung im November. Parmelins Nachfolge war an der Delegiertenversammlung nicht auf der Tagesordnung.

nzz.title: Johan Manzambi hat bereits seinen eigenen Fan-Song – und verzückt Prinz William, den Edelfan von Aston Villa
nzz.description: Der Schweizer Spielmacher hat in der Premier League voll eingeschlagen. Nicht nur der Trainer Unai Emery gerät ob Manzambis fulminanten Leistungen ins Schwärmen.

nzz.title: Angriffe im Westjordanland bringen Benjamin Netanyahu in Bedrängnis
nzz.description: Radikale israelische Siedler sollen eine amerikanische Journalistin und europäische Diplomaten attackiert haben. Selbst enge Verbündete Israels reagieren empört.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Trump gibt Wahlempfehlung für Netanyahu ab +++ Iranisches Parlament bestätigt neuen Verteidigungsminister
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Der FC Zürich scheitert im Cup-Sechzehntelfinal am FC Aarau – der frühere FCZ-Spieler Daniel Afriyie trifft doppelt
nzz.description: Die Aarauer sind für die Cup-Überraschung des Wochenendes besorgt. Der Klub aus der Challenge League setzt sich gegen den FC Zürich 2:0 durch.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Proteste in Frankreich: Demonstranten verwüsten mehrere Städte +++ Präsident Macron hält am Abend eine Fernsehansprache
nzz.description: Ende September gehen Schüler, Lehrpersonen und Gewerkschaften auf die Strasse und fordern bessere Lernbedingungen – und lösen damit eine landesweite Bewegung aus. Die neusten Entwicklungen.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die Berliner Linkspartei siegt über die mutlose politische Mitte: Dieses Sondierungspapier ist eine Zäsur für Deutschland
nzz.description: SPD und Grüne wollten mit der Linkspartei nur dann verhandeln, wenn eine Koalition unter ihrer Führung «nicht von Antisemiten abhängig» sei. Von diesem Vorsatz ist nichts mehr übrig. Das hat Folgen, auch über Berlin hinaus.

nzz.title: Mit 36 km/h durch den Wald brettern: In Bern werden erstmals die Schweizer Meister im Trendsport Graveln gekürt
nzz.description: Immer mehr Velofahrerinnen und Velofahrer suchen auf Schotterwegen Freiheit und Abenteuer. Nun entdeckt auch der Spitzensport die Disziplin.

nzz.description: Die russische Tech-Firma Yandex beherrscht den Markt. Das ist politisch gewollt – und macht Yandex zu einem formidablen Ziel für die Ukraine.

letemps.title: Avec «Portobello», Marco Bellochio raconte un autre chapitre maudit de l’Italie moderne

phys-org.title: Scientists discover a way to reverse coral bleaching at record speed
phys-org.description: For the first time, scientists have observed bleached corals on the brink of death fully recover through brief contact with healthy clones. Ghostly white corals returned to full health in a laboratory setting within seven weeks, the fastest documented recovery to date, according to a study published in Science Advances.

phys-org.title: Warming could help make the Indian Ocean a stronger climate buffer
phys-org.description: The world's oceans help slow climate change by absorbing carbon dioxide (CO₂) from the atmosphere, but how much they take up can vary throughout the year. New research, published in Geophysical Research Letters, suggests these seasonal patterns are changing across the Indian Ocean, potentially affecting how it helps to regulate Earth's climate.

phys-org.title: Close social bonds help wild jackdaws hold feeding spots but come with waiting costs
phys-org.description: Close social relationships are known to contribute to the survival of many animals, including humans. Maintaining social bonds over time, however, can also require effort and sacrifices.

phys-org.title: Japan's MMX mission aims to swipe soil samples from Mars's moon Phobos
phys-org.description: A Japanese space mission is about to launch towards Mars. But it will not land on the planet itself. Instead, the Martian Moons Exploration (MMX) mission will focus on Phobos, the bigger of Mars's two small moons.

phys-org.title: Hybrid diamond chip strengthens interactions between light and quantum bits
phys-org.description: Researchers have developed and demonstrated a new hybrid photonic platform that integrates quantum emitters with photonic devices, providing a way to reliably control the interaction between photons and quantum information carriers. The chip-based platform, which combines gallium phosphide (GaP) with a diamond substrate, could help make quantum networks more practical by providing a way to connect quantum devices over long distances.

phys-org.title: Lion droppings yield previously unknown microbial species, exposing hidden diversity inside Africa's big cats
phys-org.description: Scientists know a great deal about how lions hunt, breed and survive, but the microscopic communities living inside them have remained largely unexplored. Now, a study of wild lions in Namibia is beginning to change that, while revealing how much biology is still missing from the world's genomic databases.

phys-org.title: One million migrating raptors dodge illegal hunters above Georgia's Black Sea coast
phys-org.description: Standing on a verdant hill above Georgia's Black Sea coast, ornithologist Bart Hoekstra looked out over one of the world's greatest wildlife spectacles unfolding before him—then gunshots pierced the air.

phys-org.title: Japan to launch spacecraft on a mission to get samples from a Martian moon
phys-org.description: Japan is set to launch a spacecraft on the world's first mission to bring back samples from Phobos, one of the two small, potato-shaped moons orbiting Mars.

phys-org.title: World's oldest shipwreck discovered off coast of Turkey
phys-org.description: A shipwreck off the coast of Turkey is the oldest shipwreck in the world, our team of archaeologists believes. There's little left of the ship itself, but based on clues from its cargo—including pottery vessels—a research team I was part of has tentatively dated the wreck to around 2700–2400 B.C.

phys-org.title: What a worm's brain can teach us about sex differences in the nervous system
phys-org.description: Ever wonder what goes on inside the brain of a worm—how it processes information, responds to stimuli and perceives the world around it? Northeastern University researchers have opened up that can of worms, specifically the one containing C. elegans, a tiny roundworm that's one of the most extensively studied animals in biology.

phys-org.title: How one of Earth's worst volcanic disasters affected societies in prehistoric Japan
phys-org.description: A new international study led by Lund University examines what happened to population levels after the Kikai-Akahoya volcanic eruption in prehistoric Japan. The results paint a more complex picture than what had previously been believed. The paper is published in the journal Science Advances.

phys-org.title: Simulations explore nuclear mitigation of asteroid threats
phys-org.description: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) researchers are developing three-dimensional simulations to examine how a nuclear device could be used to deflect or potentially disrupt an asteroid threatening Earth.

phys-org.title: Quantum magic state cleanup cuts errors 40-fold in first successful hardware test
phys-org.description: Qubits, the quantum equivalent of digital bits, are fragile and prone to errors. That makes building reliable quantum computers extremely difficult. One fix has been to use traditional magic state distillation, which filters out flaws, but it is extremely resource-intensive.

phys-org.title: What an ancient volcanic eruption teaches us about resilience today
phys-org.description: When a massive environmental disaster strikes, do societies simply collapse and disappear? Or do people find a way to adapt, rebuild and recover?

phys-org.title: Hand-cranked device tells blood type and red cell levels in 1 minute
phys-org.description: When someone is badly injured, doctors urgently need two facts: the patient's blood type, so that a transfusion is safe, and their hematocrit, the share of the blood made up of red blood cells, which reveals blood loss or anemia. Hospitals measure both with large machines that need electricity and trained staff, which are often unavailable in ambulances, disaster zones or remote clinics.

phys-org.title: Salt crystals could hold clues to life beneath Enceladus's ice
phys-org.description: The ocean beneath Saturn's moon Enceladus lies under kilometers of ice, but some of its contents do reach the surface. Jets near the south pole spray out water vapor and icy particles, offering a way to investigate the hidden ocean without drilling down to it.

phys-org.title: Australian scavengers don't just eat everything and slink away. They approach a carcass like a buffet
phys-org.description: When scientists talk about scavengers, you might imagine an animal sniffing out or stumbling across a carcass, eating as much as possible and slinking away.

phys-org.title: The ambiguous costs of climate change
phys-org.description: As human activity has increased temperatures globally, determining the costs directly incurred by climate change is challenging. The effects of climate change on extreme weather events—such as hurricanes and heat waves—can be locally specific and variable, and observations and climate modeling might not accurately capture those effects.

undark.title: Podcast: Is There a Population Crisis?
undark.description: This week on the show, our hosts talk to Michael Geruso, an associate professor of economics at the University of Texas at Austin, and Jennifer Dowd, a professor of demography and population health at the University of Oxford, about population trends and fertility rates.

undark.title: Podcast: Which Animals Are Conscious?
undark.description: This week on the show, our hosts talk to Heather Browning, a philosopher at the University of Southampton in the U.K, and Deb Brown, a philosopher and the  director of the Critical Thinking Project at the University of Queensland in Australia, about which animals feel pain and more.

undark.title: Podcast: Is ADHD Actually a Disorder?
undark.description: On Entanglements this week: Barbara Franke, a professor of molecular psychiatry at Radboud University in the Netherlands, and Edmund Sonuga-Barke, a developmental psychologist and a professor at King’s College London discuss whether ADHD should be considered a disorder.

undark.title: Podcast: Should We Put AI-Enabled Tech in Our Brains?

In our first episode, we discuss neural implants and AI with Judy Illes, a professor of neurology and neuroethics at the University of British Columbia, and Joseph J. Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

proj-syn.title: A Global Euro Must First Win Over Europe
proj-syn.description: In a world of competing currency blocs, the euro is the dollar’s most credible rival. But for it to become a genuine counterweight to the greenback, the European Union must strengthen its financial foundations and expand its reach, starting with the member states that have not adopted it despite being obliged to do so.

proj-syn.title: Japan Needs Higher Interest Rates
proj-syn.description: In 2012, when Japan was dealing with chronic deflation, policymakers were right to embrace monetary easing, including lower interest rates. Today, however, Japan faces the opposite problem: a weak yen, combined with higher interest rates in the US, calls for a much tighter monetary policy.

proj-syn.title: A Middle-Powers Grand Strategy to Prevent Atrocities
proj-syn.description: Many governments have leverage to prevent atrocity crimes, yet lack the machinery to turn warnings into consistent, accountable action before it is too late. Now that three of the five permanent members of the Security Council are undercutting the postwar legal order, middle powers most close the gap.

proj-syn.title: Unleashing Africa’s Women Agripreneurs
proj-syn.description: Across Sub-Saharan Africa, women workers dominate agriculture but rarely capture the sector’s economic value. With a systematic approach to closing the gap, policymakers, NGOs, and philanthropic organizations could unlock a $1 trillion market and transform the continent’s food systems for the better.

proj-syn.title: Low Expectations for Israel’s Election
proj-syn.description: Benjamin Netanyahu has led Israel into a trap in which ever-increasing strategic commitments are outstripping the productive base that finances them, and the goodwill on which its alliances depend is being destroyed. While a new government would not transform Israeli foreign policy, it could begin to drag Israel out of its morass.

proj-syn.title: From AI Boom to Economic Bust
proj-syn.description: Contrary to tech optimists' rosy predictions, AI may prove to be a drag on growth. By concentrating wealth and economic opportunities in a few cities while destroying the low-cost jobs that have historically fueled global development, the technology could end up making much of the world poorer and more divided.

proj-syn.title: The Institutional Roots of Policy Nonsense
proj-syn.description: At a time when antimicrobial resistance threatens public health and our long-term economic well-being, tax policies favor financial engineering at the expense of developing new antibiotics. Similarly perverse incentives are at the heart of out-of-control public spending.

proj-syn.title: Is Christian Democracy Finished?
proj-syn.description: Traditionally, Christian Democrats believed that taking care of all groups in society could create a harmonious balance that would prevent instability and self-destructive infighting. But the conditions that enabled this strategy have changed, particularly in Germany, where Christian Democrats must reconnect with a different part of their history.

proj-syn.title: Independent AI Auditing Now
proj-syn.description: Recent hacking incidents confirm the need for independent scrutiny not only of what AI systems are capable of, but also of what their developers are doing to minimize harm and communicate honestly with the public. Even if AI auditing is still at an early stage, other industries have already provided a playbook.

proj-syn.title: Strict Liability for AI Executives
proj-syn.description: As an OpenAI whistleblower recently explained, AI executives have knowingly fostered a culture that “guarantees periodic failures,” the scale of which is “growing as systems get more capable.” This approach hinges on an expectation of impunity, which is why AI firms must be held legally accountable for the harm their agents cause.

proj-syn.title: Who Will Pay to Preserve Tropical Forests?
proj-syn.description: For decades, the international community has acknowledged the extraordinary value of tropical forests while failing to invest adequately in their conservation. The Tropical Forest Forever Facility, launched at last year’s United Nations Climate Change Conference, could help close this financing gap.

proj-syn.title: Why Following in Milei’s Footsteps Would Be Bad for Brazil
proj-syn.description: Far-right presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro holds up Argentine President Javier Milei’s economic program as a model for Brazil. But Milei's economic experiment has been a failure, leaving millions of Argentinians worse off and effectively turning their heavily indebted country into a client of the United States.

proj-syn.title: How Worried Should We Be About the Global Economy?
proj-syn.description: The risks to the global economy—including high inflation, soaring public debt, market concentration, and geopolitical volatility—are well known. But it is worth underscoring just how rare and dangerous it is for all of them to be salient at the same time.

proj-syn.title: How a Pause on Frontier AI Could Work
proj-syn.description: Whether the development of frontier AI should be paused is for policymakers to decide. But they should recognize that highly concentrated hardware supply chains make a pause feasible and, if implemented properly, likely to be sustainable.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Latest Gift to Putin
proj-syn.description: Unable to win his foolish war against Iran, Donald Trump blames its consequences on Ukraine and uses the lie to justify ending sanctions against Russia, thereby extending that war as well. His diesel deal with the Kremlin is less about lowering gas prices for Americans and more about submitting to Vladimir Putin.

proj-syn.title: China’s Panda Diplomacy Is Losing Its Charm
proj-syn.description: Since giving a pair of giant pandas to the Smithsonian’s National Zoo in 1972 following President Richard Nixon’s visit to Beijing, China has used panda loans as a means of projecting a harmless and friendly image globally. But it was always an act—and foreign audiences are no longer falling for it.

proj-syn.title: The Blindness of China’s All-Seeing State
proj-syn.description: China's relentless surveillance has taught people to perform obedience and loyalty, while keeping their beliefs hidden. This creates a dilemma for the ruling Communist Party: repression distorts the very information the government needs to understand society.

proj-syn.title: A Stronger Renminbi Is No Quick Fix for Global Imbalances
proj-syn.description: The near-consensus among financial commentators is that China's currency is undervalued, driving global imbalances. But the renminbi's weakness reflects weak domestic demand, and pursuing currency appreciation without addressing that issue head-on would be counterproductive for everyone.
